signal.reasoning: I can understand the economics shown here: Apple earns high, steady margins, produces substantial free cash flow, and has increased book value per share while reducing debt relative to equity. Those are signs of a strong business, though four quarters cannot establish how durable its moat will be, and a current ratio near 1 leaves little cushion. At 37.5 times earnings, the price asks a great deal of future growth; I would be comfortable owning this business for ten years, but not yet convinced I am getting a fair price.
